transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Parkview Head of IT), Leah Turner (Parkview Compliance Manager), David Ng (Parkview Platform Engineer)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on data residency, logging restrictions for financial services, and options between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Customer is leaning toward private/Dedicated due to regulatory constraints but wants clarity on audit logs, encryption, and cross-border processing.

Topics:
- GDPR/data residency (EU customer base routing)
- HIPAA implications for some loan document processing (customer has small healthcare lending portfolio)
- Logging and PII retention controls (what Redwood stores in hosted mode)
- Network architecture options (VPC peering, Private deployment, on-prem)
- Benchmarks and pilot next steps

[00:00] Sam Patel: Hey everybody thanks for joining, quick hello from me and Maya at Redwood. Um before we kick off, can I just confirm the agenda — run through compliance questions, residency, then technical constraints and next steps?
[00:22] Carlos Ramirez: Yep that sounds good. I'm Carlos, I run infra. Leah will cover compliance stuff. David is on for the network bits.
[01:10] Leah Turner: Hi all, yep we want to understand where data lives, who has access, encryption at rest, in transit, plus logs. Also need to know about deletion, retention windows, and whether metadata or query logs leave our region.

[05:00] Maya Chen: Great. I'll start with an overview. Redwood offers three modes — Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private which can be VPC-hosted or on-prem. For Hosted, our default is multi-region endpoints but tenancy is shared; for Dedicated you get isolated capacity in a region; Private gives you a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem appliance. Note I might mis-say product names, sometimes folks call Dedicated, Dedicate —
[05:30] (laughter)
[06:00] Carlos Ramirez: The line that matters is: with Hosted, do you ever move data outside the region? We have EU customers and can't have European PII processed in US datacenters.
[06:20] Sam Patel: Right, good question. For Hosted we route based on endpoint region but there are edge services that may touch metadata. We do offer region pinning for production workloads — but it is different from a full VPC private deployment. For strict EU residency we typically recommend Dedicated in an EU region or Private VPC so nothing leaves customer-controlled subnets.
[07:05] Leah Turner: And regarding logs — request/response logging, do you store full prompts and responses for Hosted? What's redaction and retention?
[07:28] Maya Chen: In Hosted by default we keep logs for debugging and product health — but there's a retention policy and we offer log redaction. For customers with tight compliance needs we have an option to disable persistent logging and only keep ephemeral traces for X hours — I should caveat that for some features like streaming and function calling we may capture metadata. We'll send the SOC2/HIPAA pack that has details.
[08:10] David Ng: On networking: if we go Dedicated, how does routing work? Can we do VPC peering or do we need a VPN? What's the egress behavior?
[08:30] Maya Chen: Dedicated can be provisioned with VPC peering or private networking depending on cloud provider. For our Managed Dedicated in AWS you can do VPC endpoints and we support route controls so egress is limited to your subnets. For Private on-prem, nothing leaves your network unless you opt-in for the control plane telemetry — and that can be blocked.
[09:12] Carlos Ramirez: OK. HIPAA — we have a small set of documents that could be PHI in loan paperwork for some healthcare clients. Does Redwood sign a BAA for Hosted? For Dedicated?
[09:30] Sam Patel: We sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted it's case-by-case — historically we've done BAAs for larger customers depending on controls. I'll include the legal template but compliance does vary.
[10:15] Leah Turner: About encryption keys — do you manage keys or can we bring our own KMS/HSM? We need separation of duties.
[10:32] Maya Chen: You can bring your own KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have a Redwood-managed KMS by default, but we do offer a BYOK path for enterprise customers — integration with AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and some HSM partners.
[11:00] (brief pause, typing sounds)
[11:30] Carlos Ramirez: Are there any known issues with KV cache and data leakage? We use prefix caching in other services and want guarantees that customer cached tokens can't be served to other customers.
[11:50] Maya Chen: Good — our KV cache is tenant-scoped in Dedicated and Private. In Hosted it's logically partitioned but there have been customer concerns historically — we can provide a technical note on cache isolation and kernel-level enforcement. We also have leakage detection tests as part of onboarding for Dedicated pilots.
[12:35] David Ng: If we go Private VPC, does the Redwood control plane still exist in Redwood's cloud? We need to avoid control plane egress for regulatory reasons.
[12:55] Sam Patel: For VPC Private we can offer a private control plane that either sits in your VPC or a self-hosted control plane instance. That gives you full control over audit logs and who can access model configs. There are some features that require outbound telemetry for updates but those can be gated behind an approval flow.
[13:40] Leah Turner: Regarding GDPR — data subject access requests — if a customer asks to delete their data, how do we ensure it's wiped from logs and training sets? We are not training models with customer data but need proof.
[13:58] Maya Chen: We do not use customer request/response data to train our models without consent. For deletion we have an API for purge that removes stored logs and metadata. For Hosted we can provide deletion certificates. For Dedicated/Private you control storage so deletion is under your control; we can provide tooling to run scrubbing jobs.
[15:30] Carlos Ramirez: What about cross-border backups? Our legal team flagged backups that may be replicated during maintenance.
[15:50] Sam Patel: Backups for Dedicated in EU will remain in-region; for Hosted some DR snapshots may be cross-region unless you opt into an in-region SLA which we can provide for EU/UK customers at higher tiers. We'll call this out in the architecture doc.
[16:40] Leah Turner: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for 7 years for certain transactions. Can Redwood provide WORM or integrate with our SIEM?
[16:55] Maya Chen: Yes we can ship logs to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, Datadog) and support immutable storage policies on your side. For Hosted we can push logs to customer-owned S3 with lifecycle management so you maintain retention/immutability. For Dedicated/Private you own the logging endpoint.
[18:20] David Ng: Performance — if we go Private hosted in our VPC, do we expect any latency delta compared to Redwood Hosted? We care about token latency for real-time support chat.
[18:38] Maya Chen: There's usually a small delta due to network hop and placement; but with Dedicated colocated in the same cloud region and with our optimized runtime (batching, KV cache), you can hit comparable p50/p95 latency. We'll run benchmarks during the pilot to measure actual numbers with your prompts.
[20:00] Carlos Ramirez: Can you explain fallback behavior — if Private control plane upgrade fails, is there a safe failover? We can't have a tenant-wide outage.
[20:20] Sam Patel: We design for graceful degradation — control plane failures won't stop the inference plane in Dedicated/Private if properly configured. We'll detail the high-availability options and maintenance windows.
[22:00] Leah Turner: Also curious about RBAC and SSO. We use Okta. Can we map Okta groups to Redwood roles and have audit around who invoked what model?
[22:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. SAML/Okta integration is supported. You can map roles and we log token-level actions for audit. For Hosted we capture username/email in logs; for Private we can integrate with your LDAP and have no username stored outside your network.
[24:00] Carlos Ramirez: Any mandatory data we need to send to Redwood support for troubleshooting? We prefer to redacted PII.
[24:18] Sam Patel: Commonly we request a sanitized transcript and some request ids. For Dedicated we can provide secure debug sessions where logs are ephemeral. We respect your redaction policies.
[25:15] (brief cross-talk)
[26:10] Maya Chen: To summarize technical recommendations given what you've said: If you require strict EU residency + long-term immutable logs + BAA, we recommend Private or Dedicated provisioned in-region with BYOK and pushed logs to customer S3. Hosted could work for non-PII workloads or dev/testing.
[27:00] Leah Turner: That aligns with our thinking. A couple of legal questions — sample BAA, and does Redwood have a subprocessor list? We need to circulate to legal.
[27:20] Sam Patel: Yes we'll send the BAA template and a current subprocessor list. Note some subprocessors change quarterly; we'll include the latest.
[28:40] David Ng: For the benchmarking session — can we test KV cache warmup behavior for our prompt templates? We see cost differences if cache is cold.
[29:00] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll simulate typical session profiles and show cost/latency differences. We'll also test quantized model variants for throughput if you're CPU-constrained.
[30:00] Carlos Ramirez: Pricing — what are the committed tiers for Dedicated? We need ballpark numbers to discuss with finance.
[30:20] Sam Patel: I'll share a pricing sheet. Typical Dedicated starts with a minimum commit for X GPUs — I'll send options for monthly vs annual with burst pools. For Private there is a license + support fee.
[31:40] Leah Turner: Any certifications beyond SOC2? ISO? PCI? We have some card transaction data in a different product line but want to know future scope.
[31:55] Maya Chen: We maintain SOC 2 and are pursuing ISO 27001; PCI is not in our core stack today but we can talk about options for tokenization and isolating card workflows using dedicated pipelines.
[33:10] Carlos Ramirez: Is there an NDA? Our legal asked for non-disclosure before we share sample PHI data for benchmarking.
[33:28] Sam Patel: We can sign an NDA — standard. We'll attach the legal contact in the email.
[34:00] Leah Turner: Two small gotchas: 1) we need proof that data won't be used for model training, 2) we need log deletion certificates for GDPR audits.
[34:18] Maya Chen: We'll provide a signed statement that we don't train on your data without permission and deletion certificates for Hosted logs on request. For Dedicated/Private you control that.
[36:00] David Ng: Network ops question — do you require specific ports opened? Our security team is strict.
[36:15] Maya Chen: We'll provide a minimal port list and IP ranges for the Dedicated endpoints. For Private on-prem there may be an installer that needs outbound to Redwood registry, which we can host locally if you prefer.
[38:00] Carlos Ramirez: Any examples of other banks you've onboarded with similar requirements?
[38:20] Sam Patel: Yes, we've done a few regional banks with EU residency — won't name specifics, but we can provide a redacted case study and a technical reference.
[39:10] (pause)
[40:00] Maya Chen: Ok, next practical steps: Sam will send the compliance packet + BAA; Maya will draft the VPC/private architecture; we schedule the benchmarking session 7/31 and David will share subnet details ahead of time.
[41:00] Carlos Ramirez: That works. Also please include log retention options and price delta for in-region-only backups.
[41:18] Sam Patel: Will do.
[42:30] Leah Turner: Anything else from Redwood?
[42:45] Sam Patel: Nothing more — thanks for the time. We'll follow up with the docs and set the benchmark calendar invite.
[44:30] Carlos Ramirez: Thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript.
